From Wiktionary, the free dictionary
See also: diplome, Diplome, diplomé, and diplômé

French

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

Learned borrowing from Latin diplōma, itself borrowed from Ancient Greek δίπλωμα (díplōma).

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): /di.plom/
  • Audio:(file)
  • Audio (France (Toulouse)):(file)
  • Audio (France (Vosges)):(file)
  • Audio (France (Lyon)):(file)

Noun

[edit]

diplôme m (plural diplômes)

  1. diploma (document issued by an educational institution testifying that the recipient has earned a degree or has successfully completed a particular course of study)

Derived terms

[edit]
  • diplômer

Related terms

[edit]
  • diplomatique

Norman

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

Borrowed from French diplôme, from Latin dīplōma, from Ancient Greek δίπλωμα (díplōma, “folded paper, license”), from διπλόω (diplóō, “to double, fold over”), from διπλόος (diplóos, “double”).

Noun

[edit]

diplôme m (plural diplômes)

  1. (Jersey) diploma
